knowledge-base.name: code-exploration
knowledge-base.triggers: explore, codebase, understand, find, where, how does, architecture, structure, dependencies, navigate, search code
knowledge-base.overview: Systematic code exploration produces reliable understanding faster than ad-hoc browsing. Techniques for navigating codebases of any size.

core-principles.principle: Structured exploration: Use systematic patterns, not random browsing
Pattern recognition: Look for recurring structures across files
Dependency awareness: Understand relationships, not just individual files
Incremental depth: Start broad, drill down as needed
Context preservation: Always note file paths and line numbers

workflow.name: Quick Overview
workflow.step: Find entry points (main, index, app, server)
workflow.output: High-level structure map, tech stack, entry points

workflow.name: Feature Understanding
workflow.step: Extract entities from the ticket or goal: file paths, PascalCase class/service names, API endpoint paths, model names

For each entity, run BOTH: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", mode="vector") to find semantically similar code, AND POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", mode="graph") to find structural neighbours (imports, inheritance, callers. Never run only one — they find different things.
Collect unique file paths from graph results into a "Files in Scope" starting map
Identify feature entry point (API route, UI component)
Map call chain through execution path
workflow.output: Files in Scope map (from graph seeds), execution flow, key files list, test locations

workflow.name: Architecture Discovery
workflow.step: Identify layer boundaries (UI, API, business, data)
workflow.output: Layer diagram, pattern catalog, integration points

layer.name: Presentation
layer.contains: Components, Views, Templates, Route handlers, Controllers

graph-rag-strategy.overview: Use both vector and graph RAG together at task start. Vector finds semantically similar code; graph finds structural neighbours via imports and inheritance. They are complementary — each finds files the other misses.
graph-rag-strategy.step: Extract entities from the ticket: file paths, PascalCase names, endpoint paths, model/table names. These are the graph seeds.
For each entity: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", project_path=..., query="[entity]", mode="vector", limit=3
For each entity: POST http://127.0.0.1:8612/search with scope="codebase", project_path=..., query="[entity]", mode="graph", limit=3
Collect unique file paths from all results. Write as "Files in Scope" to context.md. This is the starting navigation map — update it as you discover more files.
graph-rag-strategy.fallback: If the ticket has no explicit entity names, use key noun phrases from the ticket summary as seeds. If the project is not indexed, skip graph search and flag it.
graph-rag-strategy.rule: NEVER run only vector or only graph. Both calls are required. Graph traversal finds callers, middleware, and cross-file dependencies that semantic search alone misses.

large-codebase-strategies.strategy: Never read all files: Use targeted search
Start at boundaries: Entry points, APIs, tests
Follow data flow: Input → processing → output
Trust package boundaries: Don't drill into every module
Sample patterns: Find 2-3 examples, assume pattern holds
Set explicit scope boundaries before starting
Write findings as you go (don't hold in memory)
Stop when you have enough to answer the question

always-include.item: File paths: Absolute or repo-relative paths
Code context: Relevant snippets (not full files)
Next steps: What to explore next

exploration.bad: Reading files linearly: Code isn't a novel; jump around
Ignoring tests: Tests show intended usage
Missing configuration: Config often explains behavior
Skipping README: Often contains crucial context
Over-exploring: Stop when you have enough

search.bad: Too broad: *.* returns too much noise
Too literal: Missing variations in naming
Wrong language: Searching Python patterns in JS
Ignoring case: User vs user both matter

handoff-templates.handoff: "Exploration found the bug likely in these files: - src/auth/validate.ts:42 - Token parsing - src/middleware/auth.ts:15 - Middleware invocation Call chain: request → middleware → validate → [error]"
